title: An inexpensive continuous monitor for multiple human hormones

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an affordable, wearable or otherwise minimally burdensome system that continuously and simultaneously measures several human hormones during ordinary life. It would reveal how hormone concentrations rise, fall and pulse over time across multiple endocrine axes—the linked systems that coordinate hormone production and feedback. The goal is dependable measurement of endocrine dynamics outside specialist sampling facilities, rather than occasional laboratory snapshots.

The instrument would need to distinguish chemically different hormones at physiologically relevant concentrations and resolve changes quickly enough for the intended use. Its measurements must remain reliable throughout sustained operation despite interference and sensor drift. If it samples a fluid other than blood, the relationship between that fluid’s measurements and circulating hormone concentrations must be established for each hormone and use. These are requirements of the proposed broader capability; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate a completed system.

A relevant technical foundation is aptamer-enabled electrochemical sensing, in which a molecular recognition element produces an electrical response to a target hormone. The supplied 2019 study used this approach in a robotic reader for luteinizing hormone, or LH, and discussed extending it to multiple hormones and continuous sensing. It establishes an enabling approach, without establishing that this particular architecture can deliver the entire proposed monitor.

significance.text: Dependable continuous monitoring could make the timing of hormone secretion much easier to study. Hormonal pulses can carry information that an isolated concentration measurement misses. The 2019 LH paper described an assessment approach requiring peripheral blood sampling every 10 minutes for at least eight hours, followed by expensive serial immunochemical analysis. That dated example illustrates why capturing endocrine dynamics can impose substantial burdens on patients and researchers.

Conditional impact synthesis: If the proposed monitor achieved comparable biological validity with low cost and acceptable user burden, its direct consequence would be much richer observation of endocrine rhythms during ordinary life. Simultaneous measurements could show how several hormonal signals vary together, expanding research beyond isolated hormones and tightly controlled sampling sessions. Observed correlations and timing relationships would not, by themselves, establish causal interactions between endocrine systems.

Conditional clinical possibilities include detecting abnormalities missed by sparse sampling and supporting decisions that depend on hormone timing or variability. These possibilities require separate validation for each application: more measurements do not automatically produce better diagnoses, treatments or outcomes. The revolutionary potential lies in making dynamic endocrine measurement accessible and dependable; its eventual clinical reach would depend on what those measurements reliably reveal and whether acting on them helps patients. No historical comparison examples were supplied, so a stronger ranking of its revolutionary importance is not justified here.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is sustained, simultaneous measurement of multiple hormones with sufficient specificity, sensitivity and temporal resolution for the intended endocrine questions. Success with one hormone does not establish success with chemically different targets or with a panel operating together. The 2019 paper discussed hormone specificity, sensor regeneration, cost and future multiplexing, including the possibility of using multiple single-wire electrodes to measure several hormones in one sample. That proposed extension was not a demonstrated continuous multi-hormone system.

Long-term measurement also requires a stable relationship between hormone concentration and sensor output. The 2019 article identified signal drift reported for electrochemical aptamer-based continuous sensors in whole blood and discussed regeneration as an engineering concern. A practical monitor must distinguish real hormonal changes from changes in sensor behavior, maintain useful performance through repeated measurements, and control interference without relying on burdensome laboratory procedures.

Engineering synthesis: Biological interpretation is a separate barrier from analytical detection. A sweat or other non-blood sensor could accurately measure its sampled fluid while still failing to reproduce the concentration or timing of a circulating hormone. Hormone-specific relationships, delays and variation across relevant conditions therefore need testing. Simultaneous sensing, calibration, data interpretation, sustained operation and acceptable total cost must work together. The supplied 2019 study did not investigate sweat-to-blood correspondence, and the supplied material does not establish that these broader barriers have been overcome.

current_state.text: On 20 February 2019, Shaolin Liang and colleagues published “Measuring luteinising hormone pulsatility with a robotic aptamer-enabled electrochemical reader” in Nature Communications. Their RAPTER system measured LH in collected patient serum samples. A larger proof-of-concept evaluation used 441 serum samples from three patient cohorts known to have different LH concentrations and pulsatility profiles, comparing results with a clinical immunochemical assay. This demonstrated a relevant method for reconstructing LH concentration profiles and assessing pulsatility from serial samples.

Those results concerned one hormone measured after blood collection and serum preparation. They did not demonstrate continuous sensing inside the body, ordinary-life wearable monitoring or measurement across multiple endocrine axes. Continuous sensing and multiplexing appeared as future adaptations in the discussion. The supplied review’s assessment relied on full article prose and captions, particularly the clinical comparison results and Clinical samples methods; figures were not visually inspected. Figure 3 characterized the electrode and was not the principal evidence for the patient-sampling conclusion.

The reconciled research also identifies a paper attributed to Xiaochang Pei and colleagues, “A quantitative, multimodal wearable bioelectronic device for comprehensive stress assessment and sub-classification,” dated 29 January 2026. It records an earlier abstract-based account of physiological measurements combined with sweat-cortisol sensing. However, the retained PubMed page available to the supplied review contained only a cookie-access message. The review could not verify the article’s identity, measurements, continuity of operation or validation from that content. The reported findings therefore remain an unverified lead within this record; the access failure is not evidence that the findings are false.

Evidence-bound assessment: The supplied material establishes the dated 2019 technical foundation, but it does not establish the field’s overall status as of 1 November 2026. The freshness record was empty, and the retained 2026 page did not contain scientific content. Even if the earlier account of sweat-cortisol sensing is accurate, measuring several physiological modalities alongside one hormone would not alone demonstrate continuous monitoring of multiple circulating endocrine axes. This record consequently cannot determine whether the full proposed capability remains unmet throughout the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: An inexpensive, wearable or otherwise minimally burdensome system continuously and simultaneously measures a specified panel of validated hormones spanning at least two endocrine axes during ordinary life. Before testing, investigators should define the panel, monitoring duration, intended applications, acceptable user burden and total cost. The two-axis threshold is a proposed way to demonstrate breadth beyond a single hormone, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Continuous simultaneous hormone monitoring spans at least two endocrine axes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed analytical and temporal validation: Prespecify hormone-specific criteria for concentration accuracy, timing, drift and interference, and test them against reference blood measurements across the physiological and disease ranges relevant to each intended application. Any use of a different sampled fluid should include explicit validation of its relationship to circulating concentrations and timing. Testing should establish sustained simultaneous performance over the claimed monitoring period, so that isolated successful readings or separate single-hormone experiments do not substitute for the integrated capability.
completion_criteria.label: Validate sustained simultaneous hormone measurements against prespecified blood-reference criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: Independent studies should reproduce the claimed performance and report where it deteriorates or fails, including limits of the hormone panel, concentration range, monitoring duration, sampled-fluid interpretation and ordinary-life conditions. Affordability and burden should be evaluated for the complete monitoring process, including recurring supplies, calibration and specialist support where needed. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not universal performance across every hormone, person or condition.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduce performance, reporting practical boundaries and complete monitoring costs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical validation: For claims that monitoring improves care, clinical studies should show improved outcomes for at least some clearly specified monitoring-guided decisions. Analytical reliability establishes the measurement capability; clinical benefit requires evidence that using the information improves decisions and patient outcomes. These proposed criteria extend the candidate’s completion demonstration and are not requirements established by the 2019 study.
completion_criteria.label: Monitoring-guided decisions improve patient outcomes in clinical studies

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: END-04, “A predictive theory of interacting endocrine control systems,” is the closest conceptual complement. END-03 would supply time-resolved observations that could help develop and test such a theory. END-04 would seek explanations and predictions about interactions and feedback. Reliable measurement alone does not provide a predictive theory, and a theory does not establish a practical monitor.

Roster-based synthesis: END-01, “Immune-protected, renewable human islets that restore autonomous glucose regulation,” END-02, “A general platform for replacing failed endocrine glands with feedback-responsive tissue,” END-07, “Regenerate a person’s own functional pancreatic beta cells,” and END-08, “Restore ovarian endocrine function without previously banked tissue,” concern restoring hormone-producing tissue or gland function. END-03 could potentially help characterize their hormone output and feedback behavior if its validated panel were appropriate. It would measure function rather than supply replacement tissue, regeneration or immune protection.

Roster-based synthesis: END-05, “Durable, safe resetting of dysfunctional energy-balance regulation,” and END-06, “Programmable tissue-selective control of hormone action,” concern changing physiological regulation or the effects of hormones in selected tissues. Multi-hormone monitoring could potentially help assess responses, but circulating hormone concentrations alone do not fully determine tissue-specific action or demonstrate durable resetting of a regulatory system.

Roster-based synthesis: END-09, “Glucose-responsive insulin that substantially automates insulin dosing,” concerns a therapy whose insulin availability or action responds to glucose. END-03 concerns measurement and would not itself provide that therapeutic response. END-10, “Induce durable antigen-specific tolerance in autoimmune endocrine disease,” concerns changing the immune response that contributes to endocrine damage. Monitoring could potentially help assess endocrine function during either intervention, but it would not establish automated insulin dosing or antigen-specific immune tolerance. These entries remain distinct innovations.

change_log.change: Preserved END-03’s identity while expanding the explanation of simultaneous, affordable monitoring across multiple endocrine axes.
change_log.reason: The innovation concerns an integrated measurement capability; a robotic single-hormone assay or multimodal wearable alone does not establish it.

change_log.change: Added the 2019 publication date, collected-serum scope, 441-sample evaluation, three patient cohorts and clinical assay comparison.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports these details and they clarify both the achievement and its experimental boundaries.

change_log.change: Located the 2019 clinical conclusions in the clinical comparison results and Clinical samples methods, while preserving the limitation that figures were not visually inspected.
change_log.reason: The review identified these sections as more directly relevant than Figure 3, which characterized the electrode.

change_log.change: Recast the 2026 wearable result as an earlier research report whose findings could not be verified from the retained page.
change_log.reason: The review received only a cookie-access message, which supports an access limitation rather than acceptance or rejection of the scientific claims.

change_log.change: Removed the categorical implication that the supplied studies establish the broader capability remains unmet in 2026.
change_log.reason: The empty freshness record and inaccessible 2026 scientific content prevent a field-wide current-status conclusion.

change_log.change: Integrated distinctions between sampled-fluid accuracy and circulating-hormone validity, multiple modalities and multiple hormones, and temporal association and causation.
change_log.reason: These distinctions prevent narrower achievements or richer observations from being mistaken for the full capability or its downstream scientific implications.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include prespecified duration, panel, total cost, burden, simultaneous performance, hormone-specific tolerances, independent replication and sampled-fluid validation.
change_log.reason: The review’s additions make the proposed demonstration assessable while preserving their status as proposals rather than established standards.

change_log.change: Separated measurement capability from use-specific clinical benefit and explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Clinical outcomes require additional evidence, and overlap with modeling, tissue restoration and therapies does not justify merging distinct innovations.

unresolved_issues: The identity, findings and validation scope of the cited 2026 wearable study remain unverified from the retained scientific content. The earlier abstract-based account and later access failure cannot be reconciled further from the supplied inputs.
The supplied evidence does not establish the field’s overall status as of 1 November 2026 or whether another system has achieved the proposed capability.
The intended hormone panel, endocrine axes, monitoring duration, applications, acceptable user burden and definition of inexpensive remain unspecified.
Hormone-specific accuracy, timing, drift and interference tolerances, and any sampled-fluid relationship to circulation, remain to be defined and demonstrated.
Which monitoring-guided decisions would improve clinical outcomes remains an application-specific research question.
No historical comparison examples were supplied, so comparative revolutionary importance cannot be calibrated beyond the stated conditional consequences.
